PMID:34429127.topic: VTE prophylaxis after hip and knee arthroplasty
PMID:34429127.setting: 31 hospitals performing more than 250 hip and/or knee arthroplasties a year; cluster-randomised crossover trial nested in the Australian Orthopaedic Association National Joint Replacement Registry
PMID:34429127.other_findings: Statistical analysis plan for the CRISTAL trial (aspirin 85–150 mg vs enoxaparin 40 mg); recruitment stopped early after an interim analysis met the stopping rule. Protocol compliance was audited on the first 20 patients per arm, with re-education and re-audit until compliance exceeded 80%.

PMID:35638205.topic: Open fracture management against BOAST standards
PMID:35638205.setting: National Trauma Audit and Research Network (TARN) data from up to 190 NHS hospitals; registry-based incidence and quality-of-care study
PMID:35638205.standard: BOAST 4 / Open Fracture BOAST and National Major Trauma Centre Dashboard standards (e.g. debridement within 12 hours, soft-tissue coverage within 72 hours, combined orthoplastic plan, antibiotics within one hour)

cycle1.result: Of 12,170 severe open tibial fractures: median time to debridement 13.0 hours (IQR 6.4 to 20.9); debridement within 12 hours 24% overall (22% 2008–2011, 28% 2012–2015, 21% 2016–2019); soft-tissue coverage within 72 hours 4% (2008–2011) rising to 35% (2016–2019); first debridement with consultant orthopaedic and plastic surgeons present 10% (n = 1,175).

PMID:35638205.other_findings: Missing data exceeded 25% overall and reached 83–85% for some standards, limiting interpretation. Six of 13 BOAST standards declined between 2012–2015 and 2016–2019; overall open fracture incidence 2012–2019 was 6.94 per 100,000 person-years.

PMID:30825004.topic: Hip fracture national audit quality indicators
PMID:30825004.setting: Dutch Hip Fracture Audit (DHFA), nationwide registry; 60 of 81 Dutch hospitals participating
PMID:30825004.standard: Dutch guidelines 'Proximal Femur Fracture' (2016) and 'Multidisciplinary Treatment of Frail Elderly During Surgical Procedures' (2016); national guideline states every patient over 70 should receive orthogeriatric management

cycle1.result: Case ascertainment 58% (10,612 of 18,385 operated patients); variable completeness 77% (91% at discharge, 30% at 3 months); median time to surgery 18 h (IQR 7–23) for ASA 1–2 and 21 h (IQR 13–27) for ASA 3–4; 78% of operated patients aged 70 and over received orthogeriatric management.

PMID:30825004.other_findings: Describes set-up of the national audit; significant variation between hospitals on all three indicators (e.g. 29–75% of ASA 1–2 patients operated within 18 h). Only 23% of older patients were treated on a dedicated orthogeriatric ward.

PMID:36475361.topic: Open fracture time to debridement and soft-tissue cover
PMID:36475361.setting: Trauma Audit and Research Network (TARN) data from 175 hospitals (major trauma centres and other hospitals); registry cohort study
PMID:36475361.standard: Open Fracture BOAST: debridement within 12 hours and soft-tissue coverage within 72 hours

cycle1.result: Debridement within 12 hours in 2,052 patients (46%), median time 13.6 hours (IQR 6.4 to 20.9); soft-tissue coverage within 72 hours in 2,187 (63%), median 47.8 hours (IQR 15.9 to 111.5). Evening presentation (16:00 to 23:59) less likely to meet debridement standard (RR 0.56); Thursday/Friday presentation (RR 0.88/0.89) and non-MTC care (RR 0.76) less likely to meet coverage standard.

PMID:36475361.other_findings: Time to debridement was missing for 45% and time to soft-tissue coverage for 52% of patients, mostly from non-MTC hospitals. Proportion meeting the 72-hour coverage target rose from 44% to 69% between 2012 and 2015.

PMID:34748023.setting: Secondary analysis of UK Physiotherapy Hip Fracture Sprint Audit linked to National Hip Fracture Database, HES, PEDW and ONS data; hospitals in England and Wales

cycle1.result: 20% (1,026) received physiotherapy on 6–7 of 7 days in the first postoperative week. Adjusted odds ratio of discharge 1.26 (95% CI 1.19–1.33) per additional day of physiotherapy and 1.33 (95% CI 1.12–1.57) for ≥ 2 h vs < 2 h; physiotherapy type not associated with discharge.

PMID:34748023.other_findings: Authors propose a 7-day physiotherapy service totalling at least 2 h in the first postoperative week as a key performance indicator; estimated saving of 456 bed-days a year for an average hospital.

PMID:41338245.setting: Scottish Hip Fracture Audit national registry linked to national hospital and mortality records; retrospective cohort

cycle1.result: CFS completed in 8,573 of 15,546 patients (55%). Mortality aHR 1.77 (95% CI 1.52 to 2.06) for CFS 4–5, 3.01 (2.59 to 3.50) for CFS 6–8 and 9.95 (7.03 to 14.09) for CFS 9 vs CFS 1–3; one-year mortality AUC 0.72 for CFS vs 0.66 for ASA.

PMID:41338245.other_findings: CFS was a non-mandated registry variable, explaining low completion. CFS predicted return to original residence within 30 days only moderately (AUC 0.63 vs 0.61 for ASA).

PMID:38578023.setting: Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; trauma and elective orthopaedic surgery across both sites
PMID:38578023.standard: BOAST 'The Safe Use of Intraoperative Tourniquets': document exsanguination method, isolation method, skin condition, pressure and duration; pressure lower limb SBP + 70–130 mmHg, upper limb SBP + 50–100 mmHg; duration ideally < 120 min

cycle1.result: Exsanguination method documented 5.6%, isolation (shut-off drape) 2.4%, skin condition 0%; duration not in operative note 23.0%, not recorded at all 1.6%; > 120 min in 1.6%; pressure within standard in 24.3% lower limb, 34.8% upper limb and 66.7% paediatric cases.

PMID:38578023.intervention: Local presentation at trust Quality & Safety Half Day and 'PRESSURE' mnemonic posters in theatres and offices, followed by a new electronic patient record with a tourniquet section and BOAST-based auto-text proforma in the operation note.

cycle2.result: Exsanguination method documented 42.9% (p = 0.001), isolation 42.9% (p = 0.0001), skin condition 64.3% (p = 0.0001); duration not in operative note 10.2% (p = 0.0269), not recorded 0%; none > 120 min; pressure within standard 13.0% lower limb, 35.7% upper limb, 14.2% paediatric (no significant change).

PMID:38578023.other_findings: An interim re-audit in March 2022 after education alone (n = 153) showed little change (e.g. exsanguination 9.8%, skin condition 5.2%). Staff survey (n = 19) found over 50% sized tourniquets on 'whatever looks the best fit' and 31.6% did not know paediatric pressures.
